items.summary: This paper offers a candidate descriptive model based on the author’s retrospective account of internal agent-like experience during a past period of social isolation, emotional distress and perceived high cognitive load. It is a non-clinical reconstruction, not a technique, treatment or recommendation. No contemporaneous physiological, behavioral or neuroimaging measurements were recorded. The Opposition–Load–Coupling vocabulary organizes reported phases of self-talk, opposition, felt load, perceived coupling, autonomy, boundary degradation and disengagement. These are reported experiences and interpretive constructs, not demonstrated causal mechanisms. Claimed benefits and harms are unmeasured first-person reports. The Shared Value Anchor is an untested candidate predictor, not an established stabilizer or necessary condition. The case does not establish whether value conflict preceded initial boundary degradation or distinguish the proposal from a simpler load-based account. The model is situated alongside dialogical-self, Internal Family Systems, predictive-processing, imaginary-companion, writer-agency and tulpa literature. Any incremental contribution lies in the proposed coupling vocabulary and separately testable value-anchor hypothesis, not in discovering internal multiplicity or proving a new mechanism. Safety: do not intentionally induce or replicate the conditions described. This is the author’s own past experience, published at the author’s direction; no formal ethics approval or exemption is claimed. Version 4 incorporates author-adopted revisions following advisory and changed-text checks, including prior-involved AI reviewers. Those checks are not independent peer review, clinical validation or evidence of effectiveness.

items.summary: Lecture 1 formulated the recommendation problem in abstract terms: a set of users U , a set of items I , and a preference function r(u,i) that must be estimated for the pairs that have not been observed. Every algorithm studied in this course, however, operates on concrete data rather than on abstractions. The quality of a recommender system is therefore bounded by the quality, the structure, and the representation of the data from which it learns. In practice, improving the data frequently brings larger gains than changing the algorithm. A sophisticated model trained on noisy, biased, or poorly prepared data produces poor recommendations, a principle often summarized as garbage in, garbage out . This lecture therefore addresses three questions: è Which data does a recommender system collect, and what do these data really mean? è How can these data be organized and represented so that algorithms can process them? è How must the data be prepared and partitioned before a model is built and assessed? After studying this lecture, the reader should be able to: · Identify the sources and categories of data used in a recommender system; · Characterize explicit and implicit feedback, including their strengths and weaknesses; · Construct a user–item matrix and interpret its sparsity; · Represent users and items as vectors built from interactions and descriptive features; · Apply the main preprocessing operations to ratings and implicit signals; · Split a dataset correctly and avoid information leakage. The path followed by the data throughout this lecture is: Data sources → Feedback signals → User–item matrix → Vector representations → Preprocessing → Data splitting
items.title: Lecture Notes on Recommender Systems

items.summary: We present DECAF, a privacy preserving neural speech codec that obfuscates a speaker's voice while preserving linguistic content while maintaining automatic speech recognition (ASR) performance at very low bitrates, inspired by decaffeination. At the transmitter end, speech is encoded into speaker independent content embeddings, which are compressed using residual vector quantization and transmitted without any speaker related information. At the receiver, a canonical speaker embedding, shared a priori between endpoints, is used for waveform reconstruction, enabling deterministic and consistent obfuscation of a speaker's voice. The proposed framework leverages an information bottleneck applied to self supervised representations, along with a separate speaker embedding branch, to achieve effective speaker content disentanglement. We further incorporate a CTC-based auxiliary objective, encouraging content representations that are well aligned with downstream ASR tasks. We show that DECAF operating at a bit rate of 0.5 kbps achieves an Equal Error Rate (EER) of up to 43.5% for a speaker verification system, while maintaining competitive ASR performance, yielding a relative reduction in word error rate of 33.2% compared to a state of the art method.
items.title: Decaf: A privacy preserving speech codec using speaker disentanglement and canonical voice conversion

items.summary: Speech remains intelligible to listeners under heavy temporal degradation, but whether speaker identity survives is largely unexplored. We evaluate six automatic speaker verification (ASV) models, trained on temporally intact speech, and tested under three degradations that remove different combinations of temporal cues. The models form three pairs, one per architecture family (convolutional, transformer, conformer), each pairing a waveform-input with a mel filterbank-input model. All models degrade, but robustness tracks input representation rather than pretraining scale or model size. In all nine family-by-condition comparisons the filterbank-input model degrades less, with eight of nine 95% confidence intervals excluding zero, even when it is smaller or has less pretraining than its waveform counterpart. In the controlled convolutional pair, where the models differ only in input representation, the filterbank-input model's equal error rate rises from 1.1% to 17.1% under the heaviest tested degradation, against 2.9% to29.7% for its waveform counterpart.
items.title: Input Representation, Not Model Size or Pretraining Scale, Shapes Speaker Verification Robustness to Temporal Degradation

items.summary: Speaker verification (SV) performance degrades under language mismatch due to the entanglement of speaker identity with language-specific acoustic cues. To address this problem, we leverage large-scale self-supervised pre-trained models (PTMs) to learn language-agnostic speaker representations. We utilize PTMs as robust front-end feature extractors, capitalizing on their rich acoustic and linguistic knowledge acquired from vast, diverse audio data. These generalized features are then used to train a downstream speaker embedding network, effectively disentangling speaker identity from language-specific characteristics. We validate our approach on the TidyVoice2026 benchmark, which benchmarks SV under language mismatch. Our proposed system (team T02) achieves equal error rates (EERs) of 2.21% on tv26_eval-A and 2.99% on tv26_eval-U.
items.title: Cross-Lingual Speaker Verification with Self-Supervised Pre-Trained Models

items.summary: We propose DeepASA, a multi-purpose model for auditory scene analysis that performs multi-input multi-output (MIMO) source separation, dereverberation, sound event detection (SED), audio classification, and direction-of-arrival estimation (DoAE) within a unified framework. DeepASA is designed for complex auditory scenes where multiple, often similar, sound sources overlap in time and move dynamically in space. To achieve robust and consistent inference across tasks, we introduce an object-oriented processing (OOP) strategy. This approach encapsulates diverse auditory features into object-centric representations and refines them through a chain-of-inference (CoI) mechanism. The pipeline comprises a dynamic temporal kernel-based feature extractor, a transformer-based aggregator, and an object separator that yields per-object features. These features feed into multiple task-specific decoders. Our object-centric representations naturally resolve the parameter association ambiguity inherent in traditional track-wise processing. However, early-stage object separation can lead to failure in downstream ASA tasks. To address this, we implement temporal coherence matching (TCM) within the chain-of-inference, enabling multi-task fusion and iterative refinement of object features using estimated auditory parameters. We evaluate DeepASA on representative spatial audio benchmark datasets, including ASA2, MC-FUSS, and STARSS23. Experimental results show that our model achieves state-of-the-art performance across all evaluated tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in both source separation and auditory parameter estimation under diverse spatial auditory scenes.
items.title: DeepASA: An Object-Oriented Multi-Purpose Network for Auditory Scene Analysis

items.summary: This repository provides the datasets, pretrained models and generated network parameters used in the manuscript “DiffPINN: Generative diffusion-initialized physics-informed neural networks for accelerating seismic wavefield representation.” The accompanying source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/DeepWave-KAUST/DiffPINN-pub DiffPINN is a latent diffusion framework that generates initialization parameters for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) used in frequency-domain seismic wavefield modeling. A set of PINNs is first trained across diverse velocity models and their parameters are flattened into one-dimensional vectors. An autoencoder compresses the length of these vectors into multi-channel latent tensors, and a conditional diffusion model is trained on those tensors with the velocity model and source configuration as conditions. At inference, the diffusion model generates a latent tensor for a new velocity model, with a physics-based gradient correction applied at each reverse step, and the decoder turns it into a complete set of PINN parameters. The archived files are organized as follows. dataset.zip After extraction, dataset.zip contains five folders corresponding to the five stages of the framework: metatrain/ : contains meta_train.mat , the dataset used for meta-training. pinntrain/ : contains pinntrain1.mat to pinntrain2600.mat , one file per velocity model, used to train the 2600 PINNs that form the parameter dataset. aetrain/ : contains the flattened parameters of the 2600 converged PINNs, used to train the autoencoder. difftrain/ : contains the latent tensors encoded from those parameters, used to train the diffusion model. pinntest/ : contains CurveVelA.mat , Layer.mat and FlatFaultA.mat , the three test velocity models used to reproduce the results reported in the manuscript. All data are stored in MATLAB .mat format. Each .mat file contains the following variables: x_train , z_train , sx_train : the spatial coordinates and source locations of the collocation samples. m_train , m0_train : the squared slowness of the medium and of the homogeneous background. u0_real_train , u0_imag_train : the real and imaginary parts of the analytical background wavefield. x_test , z_test , sx_test : the coordinates of the full evaluation grid. du_real_test , du_imag_test : the real and imaginary parts of the numerical reference solution. The training velocity models are drawn from the CurveVel-A class of the OpenFWI benchmark dataset, resized to 101×101 with a grid spacing of 25 m and mildly smoothed. All wavefields are computed at 5 Hz. The reference solutions are obtained with the optimized nine-point frequency-domain finite-difference scheme of Jo et al. (1996). Among the three test models, CurveVelA is drawn from the training distribution, while Layer (a layered section of the Marmousi model) and FlatFaultA lie outside it. Because aetrain/ and difftrain/ are the outputs of the two preceding stages, users can start at any point in the pipeline rather than rebuilding the parameter dataset, which takes roughly 65 hours on ten V100 GPUs. trained_model.zip After extraction, trained_model.zip contains the three trained models used to reproduce the results in the manuscript: meta_trained.pth : the meta-learned PINN initialization, trained for 40000 iterations over 500 velocity models. ae_trained.pth : the autoencoder, trained for 1000 epochs on the 2600 flattened parameter vectors. diff_trained.pt : the conditional diffusion model, trained for 400000 iterations on the latent tensors. generated_weight.zip After extraction, generated_weight.zip contains the latent tensors generated by the trained diffusion model for the three test velocity models: CurveVelA_weight.mat : generated parameters for the in-distribution CurveVel-A model. items.summary: NANOROBOT-ENHANCED DIGITAL TWINS OF BRAIN STATE AT THE LIMIT A multiscale, uncertainty-aware research atlas on microrobotic observations, neural inverse problems, active model discrimination and the limits of computational brain twins. This research monograph asks whether additional microscale observations or strictly bounded reversible experiments can distinguish competing neural-state models that explain conventional measurements equally well. The twin is explicitly defined as a versioned scientific belief, not a digital person, a mind reader or a clinically validated instrument. Its objective is not maximum model complexity but improved identifiability, calibrated prediction under new conditions and faithful retention of failed hypotheses. The work develops five layers: multiscale neural and microenvironment state representation; posterior equivalence and prior sensitivity; non-clinical safe experimental design; frozen-version forking, rollback and reference ancestry; and blind prospective validation against classical state-space systems and independently specified alternatives. Its research architecture includes 30 distinct mathematical derivation plates linked to later chapters, 82 chapters with five independently paginated research sections apiece, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 revisable Phoenix Answer Embryos. A DOI evidence ledger identifies existing support for brain modeling, latent neural dynamics, experiment design and preclinical microrobot tracking while preventing those sources from being mistaken for evidence of the proposed integrated system. Key research questions include: Can two equally accurate virtual brains be separated by a small, permissible observation? How can the effect of a measurement itself be separated from neural change? When does a prior dominate the inferred brain state? Can the model predict unseen function rather than reconstruct a training signal? Can another laboratory reproduce a rejected twin and safely return to an earlier version? SCIENTIFIC STATUS AND LIMITATIONS This is a forward-looking, non-clinical research synthesis and experimental hypothesis architecture. It provides no personal medical advice, patient-specific interpretations or instruction to deliver neural interventions. Existing murine microrobot tracking and virtual-brain modeling studies do not establish autonomous neural nanorobot readout, human safety, privacy-sensitive mind inference or therapeutic efficacy. Proposed formulas, experiments, research gates and answer embryos are not newly validated biological laws or executed experiments. The work keeps independent safety vetoes, privacy, external reproducibility and explicit model retirement as first-class constraints. Research questions remain open to refutation, correction and reconstruction by future human and AI researchers.

items.summary: Fisher information metric tensors for the 41 held-out SONICOM test subjects, as used in “Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information” (D. Bassett). Code and reproduction instructions: https://github.com/domfrbassett/fisher-rao-hrtf-upsampling What the tensors are At each of the 793 directions of the SONICOM grid, the 2×2 tensor g = JᵀΣ⁻¹J describes how well the auditory cues separate that direction from its neighbours. J is the spatial Jacobian of the cues: Barumerli monaural PGE features, ILD and MaxIACCe-transformed ITD, each fitted with real spherical harmonics. Σ holds the cue noise (σ_mon = 1.25 dB, σ_ILD = 1 dB, σ_ITD = 0.569). All fields are low-pass filtered at 16 kHz before the cues are extracted. The tensor is expressed in a local tangent basis u₁ = a × r, u₂ = r × u₁, where a = z, or y when |r_z| > 0.9, and its units are d′² per rad². Contents metric_tensors.zip has one folder per subject, metric_tensors/subject_####/ , containing 25 files per subject (1,025 in total): reference_metric_tensor.mat : the dense measured HRTF. <METHOD>_N###_metric_tensor.mat : one file per reconstruction. There are six methods: SUpDEq_SH , SUpDEq_MCA , SUpDEq_NN_MCA_6dB (SUpDEq-Natural-MCA in the paper), SUpDEq_Bary_MCA_6dB , RANF and FSP_AE . Each is reconstructed from N = 100, 19, 5 and 3 retained directions. The 164 natural-neighbour and barycentric files at N = 5 and 3 have status “ not_applicable ”. The interpolation is undefined for those masks, so these files carry no tensors. Variables in each file: metricTensor : the tensors at SH order 6 [2×2×793]. familyGram : per-cue-family Gram matrices JᵀJ before noise weighting, at SH orders 4, 6 and 8 [2×2×793×3 families×3 orders]. They let you recompute the tensors with other noise values or SH orders. In reconstruction files only: crossFamilyGram : the unsymmetrised cross terms J_refᵀ J_recon, same layout as familyGram . airmByDirection : the pointwise AIRM discrepancy from the reference. Metadata: coordinates (Cartesian and azimuth/elevation in degrees), cue band, noise values (reference files only), status (“ completed ” or “ not_applicable ”) and, for not-applicable files, a message giving the reason. SHA256SUMS.txt lists a checksum for every file. Format and use The files are MATLAB v7.3 (HDF5), so MATLAB, h5py or any HDF5 reader can open them. Note that h5py reverses MATLAB’s axis order. scripts/fisher_lib.py in the repository reads them and recomputes tensors, AIRM and thresholds from the Gram matrices. To rerun the analysis scripts, unzip into results/evaluation/ so the subject folders sit in results/evaluation/metric_tensors/ . Provenance Produced with run_evaluation("tensors") from the repository above. The values are numerically identical to the tensor files behind results/evaluation/full_evaluation_summary.csv ; this run additionally stores the cross terms. The tensors are derived from the SONICOM HRTF Dataset (Engel et al., J. Audio Eng. Soc. 71(5), 2023, doi:10.17743/jaes.2022.0066). The SONICOM HRTFs are released under the MIT licence. This work develops research begun for the author’s B.Sc. dissertation at Birmingham City University.

items.summary: This technical note documents a conditional mathematical correspondence between the static spatial kernel used in conventional electromagnetic potential theory and the fixed-source gravitational potential in Lisa Doumbouya’s Harmonic Physics programme. Under supplied three-dimensional Euclidean geometry, spherical symmetry and stated boundary conditions, the derivation gives the static Green function 1/(4πr). Applying the existing gravitational source normalization yields the potential −μ/r, whose radial derivative gives the inward acceleration −μ/r². The note distinguishes potential, field amplitude, intensity, acceleration and optical measurement conversion, keeping geometric normalization separate from the distance exponent. The optical phase-ruler results are reviewed alongside the GRACE-FO forward forecasts. Calibrated reconstruction using measured phase retained micrometre-scale agreement with processed microwave ranging, while some forward models produced much larger errors. These results do not establish exponential error growth or identify a unique physical cause. The correspondence uses established mathematics and remains conditional on the supplied geometry, source calibration and physical interpretation. It does not establish an electromagnetic mechanism of gravity or derive spatial geometry from foundational Phase. The note includes the analytical proof, assumptions, evidence boundaries and requirements for a subsequent physical test. No new experimental data are introduced.
items.title: Inverse Radius Kernel and Optical Phase Registration

items.summary: This paper offers a candidate descriptive model based on the author’s retrospective account of internal agent-like experience during a past period of social isolation, emotional distress and perceived high cognitive load. The Opposition–Load–Coupling vocabulary organizes reported phases of self-talk, opposition, felt load, perceived coupling, autonomy, boundary degradation and disengagement. These are reported experiences and interpretive constructs, not demonstrated causal mechanisms. Claimed benefits and harms are unmeasured first-person reports. The Shared Value Anchor is an untested candidate predictor, not an established stabilizer or necessary condition. The case does not establish whether value conflict preceded initial boundary degradation or distinguish the proposal from a simpler load-based account. The model is situated alongside dialogical-self, Internal Family Systems, predictive-processing, imaginary-companion, writer-agency and tulpa literature. Any incremental contribution lies in the proposed coupling vocabulary and separately testable value-anchor hypothesis, not in discovering internal multiplicity or proving a new mechanism. Safety: do not intentionally induce or replicate the conditions described. This is the author’s own past experience, published at the author’s direction; no formal ethics approval or exemption is claimed. Version 4 incorporates author-adopted revisions following advisory and changed-text checks, including prior-involved AI reviewers. items.summary: SELF-CALIBRATING NANO-NEURAL INTERFACES AND REFERENCE LINEAGE AT THE LIMIT Built-In References × Drift Attribution × Independent Functional Requalification STARLI / Institute XXIII / Research Flagship 17 PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION When a long-running neural interface changes, is the cause the sensor, the surrounding tissue, or the decoder? An adaptive algorithm can restore predictive accuracy while obscuring the physical origin of its own correction. This book proposes a rigorous, falsifiable architecture for self-calibrating nano-neural interfaces that must retain the scientific history of every reference and every update. Its central axiom is that self-calibration does not imply self-certification: measurement claims, permission to change, electrode safety and functional benefit demand independent evidence. The first coupling is the existence of physically traceable internal references that can be challenged against electrically and temporally independent standards. The second is a source-aware drift-diagnostic process that distinguishes electronics gain, electrode-tissue transfer, tissue-like surrogate changes, changing source signals and model/feature drift, explicitly recording instances of nonidentifiability. The third is external functional requalification, which can reject an apparently successful update after hidden-domain testing, material or reference replacement, loss of selectivity, missing raw observations, or inability to reproduce the frozen predecessor. This research monograph is divided into seven causal layers and 82 chapters. Five major subsections of each chapter are assigned independent pages, yielding 410 separately paginated technical essays. Thirty gold mathematical derivations are linked from chapter-opening equations to discriminating experiments. The mathematics includes augmented state-space observability, nonlinear observation functions, source-separation Jacobians, Kalman innovations, impedance spectroscopy, covariance propagation, change-point statistics, conformal coverage, selective risk, hard-veto constrained update eligibility, reference-bridge covariance, exact rollback and cross-laboratory requalification. A displayed formula is a candidate analytical instrument with stated dimensions and assumptions, not a discovered biological law. Two hundred detailed Research Gates are preserved at the rear: 82 interrogate source identifiability, another 82 challenge independent physical and evidential hard vetoes, and 36 require third-party reconstruction of a frozen reference history. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose revisable architectures, beginning with the Neural Interface Calibration Passport. The Passport ties an interface's physical identity to the raw analog and digitized record, calibrated unit chain, hardware reference ancestors, model and feature checksums, reasons for changing any reference, failed updates, revoked permissions, blinded requalification and rollback. These are proposed evidence structures, not commercially validated devices. The DOI bibliography contains 18 unique external research records covering chronic intracortical signal instability, low-dimensional BCI stabilization, decoder adaptation, long-term electrode-tissue behavior, complex impedance metrology, electrochemical reference limits, neural interface materials and conformal uncertainty under covariate shift. Selected publisher and PubMed pages were consulted for source metadata. Their findings cannot establish efficacy of the new self-calibration architecture; source-specific claims and independent replication would be necessary.

items.summary: This working paper develops a relational Phase interpretation of black holes within the Harmonic Physics research programme, using general relativity, exact Kerr geometry and semiclassical black-hole thermodynamics as its physical baseline. It examines how phase organisation, temporal reference, observer accessibility and information persistence might relate to black-hole closure. Within the proposed framework, a phase-cycle is a closed relational structure that supports recurrence. Measured succession requires distinguishable relations and persistent records, while geometry and causal history are treated as observer-level reconstructions. The temporal-anchor hypothesis concerns a deeper terminal condition at which the parent domain loses the internally usable references needed to resolve further clocks and geometry. This proposed condition is kept distinct from the regular event horizon, across which local evolution continues. Observation is described through a joint observation relation among admitted source organisation, a physical channel and an observer-capable organisation. Source state, coupling and registered record retain separate roles; changes in accessibility may alter registration while the source organisation persists. The paper consolidates three bounded mathematical findings: exact Kerr ingoing and outgoing endpoints can have opposite trapped and anti-trapped orientations with the same mass and spin parameters; spherical source/exterior matching leaves the transition law undetermined; and a leading slow-rotation calculation permits the same sign of angular momentum in closing and opening configurations. These results establish compatibility within the stated geometric constructions. A physical transition mechanism remains to be derived. Black-to-white-hole models provide external theoretical comparisons. Return to the original exterior and the opening of a daughter phase are treated as distinct hypotheses, each requiring an appropriate causal structure, state map and conservation accounting. The remaining requirements include an invariant parent-relative terminal criterion, a physical Phase-to-boundary map, transition dynamics, information and entropy accounting, and a stable nonperturbative rotating completion. The paper remains a developing theoretical interpretation supported by standard-geometry comparisons and bounded symbolic checks. It does not establish a physical black-to-white transition, information recovery through evaporation or a daughter universe. Version 2.3, dated 17 October 2026, updates observation and self-nesting terminology, clarifies geodesic incompleteness and fixed-angular-momentum assumptions, and refreshes the references. The existing displayed equations and reported test results are retained. keywords: Phase Theory; black holes; event horizons; geodesic incompleteness; relational time; phase contraction; information accessibility; singularity; white holes; quantum gravity.

items.summary: This report establishes an exact conditional mathematical correspondence between a specified two-component phase model and the sine-Gordon equation appearing in a classical string-theory reduction. Developed within the Harmonic Physics Research Programme, the model uses interacting phase components labelled expansion and contraction in the proposed physical interpretation. For a continuum action with a cosine interaction, constant coefficients and equal component propagation speeds, an invertible change of variables separates the dynamics into an exact nonlinear sine-Gordon equation for the normalized relative phase and a free wave equation for the common phase. The interaction potential can also be expressed through the squared magnitude of the difference between two complex phase components. The derivation retains the full nonlinearity, extending the correspondence beyond the small-angle approximation. Direct numerical evolution of the original component fields provides a reproducible check at finite relative-phase amplitude. The reported breather benchmark reaches a peak relative-phase excursion of approximately 2.574 radians, with a maximum sampled error of approximately 6.3 × 10⁻⁹ radians over two oscillation periods. Component amplitudes remain fixed. Interaction-removal and unequal-speed controls document the failure to recover the same target when the specified conditions are changed. The string-theory connection is examined through the Pohlmeyer reduction of classical strings on R_t × S². A separate conventional kink embedding is checked against the local geometric constraints and string equations of motion. The evolved phase breather is not reconstructed as a string. The established result is a conditional correspondence between reduced classical equations; a full physical or quantum equivalence between the proposed phase model and string theory remains unestablished. Version 1.0 includes the standalone report and an accompanying reproducibility archive containing mathematical derivations, executable Python scripts, numerical settings, sampled synthetic data, control results, figures, source provenance, checksum manifests and reproduction instructions. A documented replay of the retained calculation and an AI-assisted computational audit support inspection and reuse of the reported results. items.summary: This report establishes an exact conditional mathematical correspondence between a specified two-component phase model and the sine-Gordon equation appearing in a classical string-theory reduction. Developed within the Harmonic Physics Research Programme, the model uses interacting phase components labelled expansion and contraction in the proposed physical interpretation. For a continuum action with a cosine interaction, constant coefficients and equal component propagation speeds, an invertible change of variables separates the dynamics into an exact nonlinear sine-Gordon equation for the normalized relative phase and a free wave equation for the common phase. The interaction potential can also be expressed through the squared magnitude of the difference between two complex phase components. The derivation retains the full nonlinearity, extending the correspondence beyond the small-angle approximation. Direct numerical evolution of the original component fields provides a reproducible check at finite relative-phase amplitude. The reported breather benchmark reaches a peak relative-phase excursion of approximately 2.574 radians, with a maximum sampled error of approximately 6.3 × 10⁻⁹ radians over two oscillation periods. Component amplitudes remain fixed. Interaction-removal and unequal-speed controls document the failure to recover the same target when the specified conditions are changed. The string-theory connection is examined through the Pohlmeyer reduction of classical strings on R_t × S². A separate conventional kink embedding is checked against the local geometric constraints and string equations of motion. The evolved phase breather is not reconstructed as a string. The established result is a conditional correspondence between reduced classical equations; a full physical or quantum equivalence between the proposed phase model and string theory remains unestablished. Version 1.0 includes the standalone report and an accompanying reproducibility archive containing mathematical derivations, executable Python scripts, numerical settings, sampled synthetic data, control results, figures, source provenance, checksum manifests and reproduction instructions. A documented replay of the retained calculation and an AI-assisted computational audit support inspection and reuse of the reported results. items.summary: The Voynich Manuscript exhibits strong statistical regularities, but the distinction between recoverable grammar and recoverable lexical meaning remains unresolved. This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.
items.title: Structural Decipherment Without Lexical Recovery: A Cross-Validated Morphological Analysis of the Voynich Manuscript
